rows.30:0b08:
You want to hear my story?
I see... Then shall I tell the second scary story?
My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
You know, before I tell this story, there's something I'd like to ask you.
It was {a}, wasn't it?
Do you mind?
Even if you say you do, I'll be asking anyway.
Well then, ready?{p}Are you a kind person?
rows.30:0c6c:
Heh heh heh... It takes something to answer that about yourself.
Either you're terribly sure of yourself, or you really are kind.
Well, never mind.
One look in your eyes will tell me which it is.{p}
rows.30:0d20: Are you someone who can keep any promise, whatever it is?
rows.30:0d70:
I see.
What a wonderful person you are.
Everyone must be very fond of you.
Someone like you is rare. A precious thing.
This is the first time I've ever met anyone like that.
Well then, let me ask you one more question.
...{a}.{p}
rows.30:0e44:
Are you the type who can take other people's advice to heart?
Even when your own opinion is different from theirs.{p}Well?
rows.30:0eb8: I can take it to heart
rows.30:0eec:
Ufufu... I just knew you'd answer that way.
You truly are the perfect human being.
I'm so happy to have met someone like you.
I hope we'll know each other for a long time to come.
Ufufufufu...{p}
rows.30:0fac:
This is the story of a tragedy that one boy happened to stumble into.
That day, he had been kept late for a make-up class.
Let's see, his name was... yes, for now, let's call him this.
{b} {a}.
It's a nice name, isn't it?
I'm sorry.
I don't know that boy's name either, you see.
So I'll borrow your name for him.
{b} {a}.
...It's a lovely name, truly.{p}
rows.30:111c:
The make-up class went like this: they were handed a worksheet, and whoever solved the problems on it could go home.
There were quite a few hard problems on it.
They weren't the kind you could solve easily.
And they were the sort of students who end up in make-up classes in the first place, you know.
Not exactly the type who love to study.
So they scribbled down any old answers and went to show them to the teacher.
Then they asked the teacher what to do, and hurried off home.
I suppose the teacher understood how it was, too.
Well, it was a make-up class in name only.
But he was different.
He sat down to the worksheet in earnest.
He wasn't the kind of person who breaks a promise.
Even if it's only a teacher, once you've made a promise, you have to keep it, don't you?
Just like you, really.
So he stayed behind alone in the classroom, trying to solve it to the very end.
Problems he couldn't find so much as a hint for, however hard he thought.
"What, you're still here?
I forgot all about you. You can go home now, {a}."
The teacher had been sure everyone had already gone home.
The classroom light was on, so the teacher looked in, suspicious, and found one student still there.
Awful, isn't it?
Well, since the teacher had given permission, he got ready to go home, and when he happened to look around, it had already gone completely dark.{p}
rows.30:1540:
Everything around him had gone dead quiet.
No one was there.{p}
rows.30:1588:
He had been left all alone in the dark school.
The only light came from dim fluorescent lamps, glowing so weakly they seemed about to go out.
There was only the dry clack, clack, clack of his footsteps echoing; no other sound could be heard.
The students who played in the schoolyard after class, the students who worked up a sweat at their clubs... none of them were left.
He glanced at the clock: eight thirty.
It had gotten so late that even he was surprised.
His classroom was on the third floor of the new school building.{p}
rows.30:1700:
In front of him were stairs leading down to the second floor, and at the far end of the hallway stretching straight ahead was another staircase down to the second floor.
Whichever way he chose, the distance to the school gate wasn't much different.{p}Which one would you choose?
rows.30:17c4: Take the stairs right in front
rows.30:17dc: Take the stairs at the end of the straight hallway
rows.30:1808:
I see, so that's the way you choose.
Heh heh heh... He did the same.
He decided to go through the long hallway and down the stairs at the far end.
That was the way he always went home.{p}
rows.30:18c4:
A long, straight hallway is truly frightening to walk at night.
The lights are few and far between, so your feet slow down on their own.
Even when you think you're hurrying, walking fast, somehow you end up slower.
"That's weird."
He muttered it under his breath.
For some reason, the hallway felt longer than usual.
Normally he'd have reached the end long ago and be heading down the stairs by now.
And yet the hallway just went on and on.
He walked and walked, and though he could see the stairs ahead, they never got any closer.
Thinking this was strange, he looked back...{p}
rows.30:1aa4:
There was proof, all right, of how far he had walked.
He really had covered as much of the hallway as he thought he had.{p}
rows.30:1b0c:
Thinking it was odd, he faced forward again, and a long hallway still stretched out ahead of him.
"Was this hallway always this long?"
He tilted his head, puzzled.
It was his first time walking through the school at night, so maybe he just couldn't judge the distance.
He tried telling himself that, too.
But even so, something about it gave him the creeps.{p}
rows.30:1c14: What will you do?{p}Will he keep going down the hallway?
rows.30:1c60: Turn back to where he started
rows.30:1c94:
"This is definitely weird."
Muttering to himself, he decided to turn back.
Somehow he sensed it would be dangerous to keep going.
But once he turned back, he couldn't get back to where he'd been, no matter how long he walked.
He was sure he had walked farther than before, and yet he never managed to reach the place he started from.
"What on earth is going on?"
He turned around once more.{p}
rows.30:1df8:
The hallway still stretched on and on.
Ahead of him and behind him, the long hallway ran on for exactly the same distance.
It felt as if the fluorescent lights had grown dimmer than before.
The light was so weak now that he couldn't see the end of the hallway.
Beyond the gloom, he could only vaguely sense the stairs.
And even that was a faint, uncertain sense.{p}
rows.30:1f50:
"Aaaaaaaagh!"
He screamed at the top of his lungs to drown out his fear, and ran.
He ran like a madman.
Forgetting all about the rule against running in the halls.{p}
rows.30:1fec:
"Ow!"
Maybe he'd strained too hard, because his own momentum sent him sprawling.
"Owww..."
Luckily, he wasn't hurt.
He'd only banged his elbows and knees hard, and he managed to stand.{p}
rows.30:20a4:
He got up and looked around once more... It didn't feel as if he'd gotten any farther at all.
However he looked at it, he was still right around the middle of the long hallway.
To be precise, both ends were wrapped in darkness by now, so he couldn't see them clearly.
He strained his eyes and took a good, hard look down the long hallway once more.
Even so, the dim hallway would never show him what lay beyond, in the darkness.
But as he strained his eyes, he froze in shock.{p}
rows.30:2304:
What will you do?
Will you run?{p}Or else...
rows.30:235c:
It was creepy enough as it was. There was no way he could go near something so incomprehensible.
{a} ran.
Fighting the feeling that his legs would give out, he ran for his life.
But no matter how far forward he went, the hallway wouldn't end.
He ran until he was out of breath, ran and ran and ran with everything he had, until at last he collapsed where he was.
It was agony; he felt like he would choke.
He coughed so violently that with every breath it felt as if his heart would come up along with it.
Even so, his position hadn't changed.
It was like running the wrong way on a conveyor belt.{p}
rows.30:255c:
Suddenly, there was a sound behind him.
The rustle of something moving.{p}
rows.30:25a8:
He felt sweat break out all over his body.
...What's wrong?
Isn't your face breaking out in sweat?
This isn't about you, you know.
This is the story of the other {a}.{p}Will you turn around?
rows.30:2720:
And then, what do you think happened?
Up ahead, he could see that black shadow from before!
He'd run away from that black lump, yet somehow it was in front of him.
Thinking it was strange, he slowly looked back.{p}
rows.30:27dc:
And then... it was behind him too.
That black, squirming, wriggling thing.{p}
rows.30:2834:
He couldn't stop his body from shaking and trembling.
After all, there was no escape now.
Hell if he went forward, hell if he went back.
Whichever way he went, he couldn't escape that black lump.{p}What will you do?
rows.30:2904: Huddle down right where he is
rows.30:2924:
He gathered his courage and set off, one step at a time.
More than courage, maybe it was closer to resignation.
He still couldn't see the end of the hallway, but he could tell the black thing was gradually getting closer.
In time with his slow steps, the thing began to take on a clear shape.{p}
rows.30:2a44:
It was a girl.
A girl in a school uniform was sitting there, huddled against the wall.
All at once, his fear was blown away.
He let out a sigh of relief and ran over to her.
What feels frightening alone feels reassuring when there are two of you.{p}
rows.30:2b38:
...She was crying.
She had her face covered, and all he could hear was her sobbing.
"What's wrong?
Did something happen to you here?"
He called out to her.
Through the gaps between the hands covering her face, she peered up at him with two bulging eyes.
"...My leg... my leg hurts so much I can't walk.
...So I'm resting.
...Please... help me."
She murmured it in a tiny, broken voice.
She had gently drawn her legs up, as if to protect the one that hurt.{p}
rows.30:2d08:
Don't you think it's strange for a girl to be in a place like this, all by herself?
You do, don't you?
What will you do?
Will you help her?{p}Or will you leave her be?
rows.30:2dbc: Leave her there and run away
rows.30:2de0:
What?
What did you just say?{p}Tell me once more.
rows.30:2e34: Leave her there and run away
rows.30:2e58:
I hope I didn't hear you wrong...
Did you just say you'd run away and leave an injured girl all alone?
That's what you said, isn't it?
You said it yourself a minute ago, that you were kind.
Or was that wrong?
Or have my ears gone funny?
I'm sure I heard you say it.
You're kind, aren't you?
Then help her.
I absolutely hate being lied to.
When someone lies to me, it makes me want to kill them.
Understand?
If you lie again, I'll kill you.
Don't you dare lie.{p}
rows.30:302c:
You're kind, after all.
You're going to help her.{p}
rows.30:306c:
"Are you okay?
I'll carry you on my back."
You gently helped her up and carried her on your back.
And she said:
"...Thank you.
...Don't let go of me."
You're kind, after all.{p}You know what you answered, don't you?
rows.30:3160:
Right.
That's what you answered.
Because you're a kind person.
Of course you did.
And then you slowly began to walk.{p}
rows.30:31e8:
Her body was cold, but she was very light.
So light it felt as though you weren't carrying anyone at all.
Even so, you could feel her thin hands winding around your neck.
Not being alone gave you just a little courage.
But the end of the hallway wasn't getting any closer.{p}
rows.30:32f4: It didn't feel like you were moving forward at all.{p}
rows.30:332c:
What's more, you began to hear a strange noise behind you.
Come to think of it, there had been a black lump at the other end of the hallway too, hadn't there?
In the end, you never found out what it was.
Maybe that was what was making the noise.
Should you turn around, or not... you couldn't decide.{p}
rows.30:3414: Just then, her breath brushed against your ear.{p}
rows.30:344c:
"...Don't turn around.
You mustn't turn around.
If you turn around, something terrible will happen...
Whatever you do, you mustn't turn around."
Unlike her cold body, her breath was lukewarm.
A nasty breath that tickled your ear.
As if to escape that breath, you dropped your gaze.
And then your eyes fell on her hands.{p}
rows.30:3570:
You were so startled you nearly threw her off.
Her hands were dry and withered, just like a mummy's.
Thin hands, with a single layer of skin clinging to the bone almost apologetically.
The fingers seemed to be nothing but bone.{p}
rows.30:3644:
"What's wrong?
You're shaking.
Are you cold?
If you're cold, I'll warm you up."
The voice whispering in your ear was very gentle.
Even so, it also seemed hoarse somehow, like the voice of a withered old woman.
Now and then her hair brushed your cheek, and it was pure white.
When you'd helped her up, it should have been long black hair, sleek and damp, yet what you saw now was white hair that stood out starkly against the darkness.{p}
rows.30:37a8:
Who on earth was it you were carrying on your back?
Maybe it wasn't even human.
If you turned around, you'd know the answer.
What will you do?{p}Will you turn around?

notes: 30:111c: teacher's gender unstated; avoided pronouns ('the teacher').
